Phase 5 — hierarchical ex-ante GPU power¶

tl;dr¶

L0 observed best total MAE 283.5 W on 565 runs (CatBoost, T-total); L1 observed best total MAE 202.7 W on 565 runs (XGBoost, G-perGPU); L2 observed best total MAE 163.0 W on 448 runs (HistGradientBoosting, G-perGPU). These own-support minima are not matched-support feature gains. All 224 cells are complete. Best-of-level has winner selection bias; historical Phase4 confirmatory is not reused as blind evaluation.

Context & Methods¶

GPU-side stable high-load text LLM inference only. L0/L0A/L1 preserve565 runs; higher support is based on semantic availability. Eight frozen candidates per nonbaseline learner, five model-group outer folds and three inner folds. Both target strategies select hyperparameters on reconstructed total watts.

Key Assumptions¶

Hardware profiles are H100/B200 reference proxies. Missing is distinct from structural N/A. Physics excludes unsupported MLA/hybrid and unknown KV dtype. Adjacent effects use matched supports.

Results¶

Information and observed accuracy¶

Supports above L1 differ; use paired increments rather than this curve for feature-value claims.

GPU-count scaling and calibration¶

Average per-GPU error is aggregate error divided by card count, not a per-card measurement.

Takeaways¶

Use same-support paired estimates for information gains; compare both reconstructed total and average per-GPU errors for target representation. Candidate choices are engineering development fits without external validation. Stress tests are post-hoc and never feed back into feature/algorithm/hyperparameter decisions. The Chinese scientific report answers RQ1–RQ8 and records coverage, search-budget and winner-selection limitations.
